core_obligations: Induction set-up (proof lines 15212-15232): the case q = 0 is the h^0 lemma for the henselian pair; for q >= 1 assume the result in all degrees < q, choose an injection F -> F' of torsion abelian sheaves with cokernel Q, and place the two associated long exact sequences over X and over Z in one commutative diagram with exact rows.

Injectivity (proof lines 15234-15242): if xi in H^q(X, F) is nonzero, apply the effacement lemma with Z = X to choose F' so that xi maps to zero to the right; then xi is the image of an element of H^{q-1}(X, Q), and bijectivity in degree q-1 forces xi to survive in H^q(Z, F|_Z).

Surjectivity (proof lines 15244-15252): given xi in H^q(Z, F|_Z), apply the effacement lemma with the given Z to choose F' so that xi maps to zero to the right; then xi is the image of an element of H^{q-1}(Z, Q|_Z), and bijectivity in degree q-1 exhibits xi as the image of the vertical map.
Together the two halves give the comparison in degree q, completing the induction (statement lines 15204-15209).
proof_roadmap: Prove the q = 0 case by the h^0 henselian-pair lemma and induct on q.
Compare the two long exact sequences attached to a chosen injection of torsion sheaves.
Efface an arbitrary class by enlarging the coefficient sheaf — with Z = X for injectivity and with Z = Z for surjectivity — and finish with the induction hypothesis in degree q-1.
difficulty_reason: The theorem is Gabber's henselian-pair comparison H^q_etale(X, F) = H^q_etale(Z, F|_Z) for torsion sheaves (statement lines 15204-15209). The proof (proof lines 15211-15256) is a degree-by-degree induction: the case q = 0 is the h^0 henselian-pair lemma, and the step compares the two long exact sequences coming from an injection of torsion sheaves, the injection being chosen by the effacement lemma — with Z = X for injectivity and the given Z for surjectivity — so that the induction hypothesis in degree q-1 closes both halves. H2: one standard induction with an effacement input, written out in full.
